agency: ICE Homeland Security Investigations, with the DHS Center for Countering Human Trafficking
headline: 905 arrests of suspected human traffickers; 180 victims rescued, 30 of them children
what_the_number_is: An arrest count for a single operation. DHS publishes no breakdown of how many of the 905 were charged with trafficking offences rather than other offences encountered during the operation, and no conviction figures.
for_scale: HSI's own FY2024 report records 1,686 trafficking investigations producing 2,545 arrests across the whole year — so one operation produced roughly a third of an annual arrest volume in a few weeks.

operation: The capacity question: where an arrest surge goes
agency: ICE detention system (analysed by the Vera Institute from ICE's own published data)
headline: More than 70,000 people held in ICE detention on a single day in January 2026 — above the previous 2019 peak — with about 444,900 detention bookings since January 2025
what_the_number_is: Vera's count of facilities in active use (456, February 2026) is more than double the 220 ICE publicly acknowledges on its website; 152 facilities opened and 170 previously closed ones reopened since January 2025. Whether constitutional standards are being met inside that expansion is litigated, not settled: courts and oversight bodies are the record for conditions and due-process claims, and this register reports filings and rulings, not conclusions of its own.
for_scale: An arrest surge is only half a fact. The other half is capacity and process: where people are held, for how long, acknowledged where, and with what access to counsel and hearings. Each of those is a countable quantity some body publishes or conspicuously does not.

operation: When sweep cases reach a courtroom
agency: US Attorney's Office N.D. Illinois (Operation Midway Blitz prosecutions)
headline: Of 33 known federal defendants charged with non-immigration crimes tied to Chicago's Operation Midway Blitz, 25 have been cleared — charges dismissed, grand juries refusing to indict (at least three refusals), one acquittal at trial — against 2 guilty pleas and 5 deferred-prosecution agreements.
what_the_number_is: Adjudication outcomes for the criminal charges that accompanied one sweep, per the Chicago Sun-Times case tracker (updated 2026-08-10). It is one operation in one district, not a national statistic — no body publishes one.
for_scale: This is the difference between an arrest count and an outcome count in practice: the announcement is the arrest number; what survives a grand jury and a judge is far smaller, and nobody aggregates that nationally.
